content.value_statement: Unread inboxes hide important messages and slow daily planning. This skill summarizes Gmail unread mail with sender, subject, date, labels, and query controls.
actual_capabilities: Shows unread Gmail messages with sender, subject, and date.
Limits the number of displayed messages with the `--max` flag.
Filters messages with Gmail search syntax through the `--query` flag.
Includes Gmail label names when the `--labels` flag is used.
Documents table output by default and an example JSON output workflow.
limitations: Requires the `gws` command line tool and configured Gmail authentication.
Only summarizes messages; it does not modify, archive, send, or delete email.
Filtering depends on valid Gmail search query syntax.
Shared authentication and global flag guidance is referenced from a sibling skill file.

use_cases.title: Start a Workday Inbox Review
use_cases.description: Get a short unread Gmail summary before choosing which messages need attention first.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Executive Inbox Digest
use_cases.description: List recent unread messages with senders, subjects, dates, and labels for a quick review session.

use_cases.title: Find Project-Specific Unread Mail
use_cases.description: Use Gmail search queries to focus triage on a project, sender, or label.

prompt_templates.title: Show My Unread Mail
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my unread Gmail inbox summary with the default settings.

prompt_templates.title: Limit the Inbox Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Review fewer messages during a short planning session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the 10 most recent unread Gmail messages and include the sender, subject, and date.

prompt_templates.title: Filter by Sender
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on unread messages from one person or team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize unread Gmail from my manager with a Gmail search query, then group the results by sender.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Targeted Label Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage for a project or workflow label.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a targeted unread Gmail triage for my project label, limit it to 25 messages, include labels, and flag likely follow-ups.

output_examples.input: Show my unread Gmail inbox summary.
output_examples.output: Unread Gmail summary: 12 messages. Top senders include Finance, Product Ops, and a customer contact. Two subjects appear time sensitive.

output_examples.input: Summarize unread mail from my manager and include labels.
output_examples.output: Unread messages from your manager: 3. Labels include Leadership and Planning. The newest message is from this morning.

output_examples.input: Find unread project messages and limit the list to five.
output_examples.output: Project unread summary: 5 messages. Senders include design, engineering, and vendor contacts. Dates range from yesterday to today.

best_practices: Confirm Gmail authentication before asking for a triage summary.
Use narrow Gmail queries when reviewing sensitive or high-volume inboxes.
Start with a small maximum result count before expanding the review.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to send, delete, archive, or modify messages.
Do not paste sensitive email content into prompts unless it is required.
Do not rely on broad queries when a sender, label, or date filter is known.

faq.question: Does this skill change my Gmail messages?
faq.answer: No. The documented triage command is read-only and shows a summary of matching unread messages.

faq.question: What Gmail data can appear in the output?
faq.answer: The summary can show sender, subject, date, and optional label names for matching messages.

faq.question: Does it require Google Workspace setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the `gws` command line tool and Gmail authentication configured for the account.

faq.question: Can I search for specific unread messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Gmail search syntax with the query option to filter by sender, label, date, or terms.

faq.question: Can it show labels?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented labels option includes Gmail label names in the output.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the local prerequisites are available.
